idiom_name: CompositionLocalProvider(LocalSelect provides scope) with content: @Composable () -> Unit slots
implementation_notes: Compose supplies both halves: the parent takes its children as a content slot (content: @Composable () -> Unit, so the call site decides the markup) and publishes the family's scope through CompositionLocalProvider, which children read with LocalSelect.current - no parameter is threaded through the call site, and recomposition is automatic because composition re-runs when state changes. Prefer a dynamic local (compositionLocalOf) when readers must be tracked, and give it a default that throws so a misplaced child fails loudly instead of silently reading a stale default - Compose resolves locals during composition, so capturing one in a long-lived lambda yields a snapshot rather than live state.
pitfalls: compositionLocalOf tracks reads and recomposes only the readers; staticCompositionLocalOf is cheaper but invalidates the whole subtree on change - choose deliberately.
A default provider value masks misuse; use error(...) as the default so an Option outside Select fails with a message instead of rendering nothing.
Locals are read during composition only, so storing LocalSelect.current in a remembered lambda or a view model captures a stale snapshot.
Reading a local in a hot loop or in every item of a large lazy list adds provider lookups; hoist the scope into a parameter for performance-critical paths.

variants.name: Classic View system: custom ViewGroup owning child views
variants.implementation_notes: The retained View system achieves the same shape imperatively: a custom ViewGroup owns the selection, children declare themselves by being added (addView) and by being Checkable, and the parent walks getChildAt to enforce exclusivity and to update styling - the shape of RadioGroup with a parent-managed checked id. What it lacks is automatic re-composition: every state change must invalidate the affected children explicitly, and the selection must be hoisted into a ViewModel or saved state to survive configuration changes. Use it in existing Views codebases; new Compose screens should use the CompositionLocal variant instead of hand-mirroring it.
variants.idiom_name: custom ViewGroup owns the selection and walks its child views; children are Checkable views
pitfalls: Children added after the parent's state was initialized are not covered unless the parent re-derives its index mapping on every layout pass.
View state is lost on configuration change; hoist the selection into a ViewModel or saved state, or the family resets silently.
A custom ViewGroup needs accessibility delegates (or Checkable children) for screen readers to announce the selection and its group semantics.
Walking getChildAt couples the parent to the child view order - keep the mapping from child identity to value explicit rather than positional if views can be reordered.
